about: Offline retrieval regression suite (T8.5). Every text here was written for these tests; none comes from an article (copyright policy rule 8). Each section becomes one chunk, <source id>-<section number>. A question's expected list holds the chunk IDs it must find in the top RETRIEVAL_TOP_K; an empty list means the coverage gate must return nothing; known_missed lists the expected chunks today's pipeline does not find (a known limit), and only_topic a topic every chunk found must carry. The recorded rates are what the pipeline gave on 2026-11-09 (T8.5), rounded down to four decimals: 8 of 9 expected chunks (the known miss is the ninth) and 2 of 2 off-topic questions with nothing back; the suite fails when a rate drops below them. Raise a rate when a change finds more; lower one only as a decision recorded in docs/TESTING.md.

1.title: Protein over the day
1.text: Eating protein at three or four meals spreads the protein supply over the day.

1.title: Protein in the evening
1.text: A protein snack in the evening adds to the protein total of the day.

1.title: Protein at breakfast
1.text: Breakfast is often low in protein, so adding eggs or yogurt raises the protein of the first meal.

2.title: Creatine loading
2.text: A creatine loading phase takes a larger daily creatine amount for about a week, to support strength.

2.title: Creatine maintenance
2.text: After loading, a smaller maintenance dose of creatine keeps the stores full and supports strength.

2.title: Creatine and strength
2.text: Creatine raises the stores used in short, hard efforts, which supports strength.

2.title: Creatine forms
2.text: Creatine monohydrate is the form most studied; other forms add no extra strength.

2.title: Creatine tolerance
2.text: Creatine at usual doses was well tolerated in the trials that measured strength.

2.title: Creatine responders
2.text: Some people store more creatine than others, so their strength response varies.

3.title: Creatine with lifting
3.text: Creatine with lifting helped lifters get stronger, with more muscle and a higher training volume.

4.title: Caffeine before a session
4.text: A caffeine supplement about an hour before a session can lift performance; coffee works too.

4.title: Caffeine and sleep
4.text: Caffeine late in the day can shorten sleep, so a daily supplement is best taken early.

5.title: Velorin
5.text: Velorin, a made-up compound named only in this test, had no effect on sleep, caffeine use, water intake or soreness.

6.title: Recovery after a hard session
6.text: Recovery after a hard session takes one to three days, and soreness fades over that time.

6.title: Soreness
6.text: Soreness peaks a day or two after an unfamiliar session and then eases; recovery is gradual.

6.title: Recovery and food
6.text: Recovery is supported by enough protein and carbohydrate after training.

6.title: Recovery and sleep
6.text: Recovery is helped by regular sleep.

7.title: Active recovery
7.text: Light activity on recovery days may ease soreness.

7.title: Recovery markers
7.text: Lifters can track recovery by how sore they feel and by bar speed.

7.title: Recovery and stress
7.text: Life stress can slow recovery from training.

8.title: Protein after a session
8.text: A serving of protein after a session, alongside carbohydrate and water, starts the repair.

9.title: Protein amount
9.text: Daily protein targets for lifters are often given per kilogram of body weight; protein needs rise in a deficit.

9.title: Protein sources
9.text: Protein from milk, eggs, meat or beans all counts toward the protein total; a protein supplement is only a convenience.

9.title: Protein quality
9.text: Protein quality depends on the amino acids a protein supplies.

10.title: Rest between sets
10.text: Longer rest between sets lets lifters keep the load and the repetitions up across sets.

10.title: Training frequency
10.text: Training each muscle twice a week is a common frequency for the same weekly volume.

11.title: Easy days
11.text: Easy cycling the morning after heavy lifting, with some water, may ease stiffness.

11.title: Fluids
11.text: Drinking water through the day keeps fluid balance; a creatine supplement does not change this.

12.title: Fat intake
12.text: Dietary fat should not drop too low in a calorie deficit.

12.title: Energy balance
12.text: A small calorie surplus with lifting supports muscle gain; a daily creatine supplement cannot replace food.

questions.why: Only keyword search knows the made-up word; vector search alone ranks six recovery chunks ahead of it.
Six chunks of source 2 rank ahead of source 3's; the per-source cap of three lets source 3 in.
Both of source 2's loading and maintenance chunks belong in the list; a cap of one pushes the second out.
The plan asks for 2024 or later; without the filter, older protein chunks push source 8 out.
A training-only plan whose year filter finds nothing is searched again on the training topic alone: it finds 10-0, and every chunk it returns carries that topic (only_topic).
